findings.title: a create with fields lands the PO in "Released", skipping its whole lifecycle
findings.description: a create with fields lands the PO in "Released", skipping its whole lifecycle
findings.detail: The UI creates an empty record (responses: []) and PATCHes fields in one at a time; that record comes back status "0" (Draft). Sending the same fields in a single create_row instead comes back status "3" (Released) — the suite never sends status at all, it is in skipFields. So a populated create silently skips Draft, In Approval and Submitted. A released PO has nothing left to approve, which is the real cause of the bare 422 "Invalid Approval" on submit. Not reproducible by hand: the UI cannot release a PO at creation.
findings.note: blocks the whole approval flow end to end; nothing downstream can be tested until it moves
findings.evidence: captured UI create_row (responses: 0) -> status "0" Draft; `npm run po -- --client decathlon` create_row (12 fields, no status) -> status "3" Released, record Z05kY2Rj

findings.title: state_code is accepted then silently discarded
findings.description: state_code is accepted then silently discarded
findings.detail: state_code is mandatory and was sent as a valid widget_data_mappings record uuid ("a1hnZE5k", the value existing POs carry). The create returns 200 and the field reads back absent. A mandatory field accepted and thrown away leaves the document permanently incomplete with no error to act on.
findings.evidence: create payload for record Z05kY2Rj included state_code; field_responses has no value for it

findings.title: omitting app-version silently returns a reduced payload
findings.description: omitting app-version silently returns a reduced payload
findings.detail: The platform selects a response serializer from the app-version header. With no such header it answers 200 but strips every step and approver uuid, so a document cannot be approved and the cause is invisible — the call looks successful. Same effect on the approval-flows list, which switches between numeric ids and encoded uuids. The suite now always sends app-version.
findings.note: worked around in the suite by always sending app-version — decide whether the default should be the full payload
findings.evidence: measured: no header -> approver.uuid undefined; 9.4.349 -> uuid present

findings.title: no way to ask which approval flow applies to a document
findings.description: no way to ask which approval flow applies to a document
findings.detail: Decathlon has 75 active p2p_create_po flows, every one conditional and several sharing the same name, so a flow cannot be identified by name. /approval_flows/applicable returns 570 "Approval Flow not found". The only way to learn the applicable flow is to write to the record and read approval_applicable + approvals back off the response.
findings.note: API gap rather than a defect — raised as a request
findings.evidence: probed live; traced through the captured UI session
